outline.chapter_title: Introduction: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion via Finetuning
outline.description: Motivates the need for controllable text-to-image generation and frames finetuning as the key problem. Introduces Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) and its constrained variant (COFT) as principled, efficient methods to adapt pretrained diffusion models while preserving semantic generation ability.
subtopics: Limits of text-only guidance in diffusion models (GLIDE, Imagen, Stable Diffusion)
Two target tasks: subject-driven generation and controllable generation
Finetuning desiderata: training efficiency and preservation of generalizability
Shortcomings of standard finetuning and adapter-based updates (small LR, Euclidean proximity assumptions)
Contributions overview: hyperspherical energy preservation, orthogonal transformations, stability via COFT, new controllability metrics, and empirical gains

outline.chapter_title: Geometry and Semantics: Hyperspherical Energy and Angular Representations
outline.description: Builds the geometric foundation underpinning OFT by explaining why angles between neurons encode semantics and how hyperspherical energy captures layer-wise relational structure.
subtopics: Angular similarity as a semantic measure (cosine similarity, angular margin literature)
Definition of hyperspherical energy: pairwise relationships of normalized neurons
Why Euclidean weight distance is an incomplete preservation metric
Toy autoencoder study: magnitude vs angle information and semantic reconstruction
Invariance of hyperspherical energy under common orthogonal transformations
Intuition: Fourier magnitude vs phase analogy and semantic preservation

outline.chapter_title: Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): Core Method and Intuition
outline.description: Presents OFT as learning a shared orthogonal transform per layer to preserve pairwise neuron angles, thereby maintaining hyperspherical energy and semantic competence while adapting to downstream tasks.
subtopics: Formulation: W = R · W0 with R orthogonal; forward pass change and identity initialization
Objective equivalence: minimizing hyperspherical energy difference to zero via orthogonal transforms
Why OFT modifies directions (semantics) while preserving structural knowledge
Why OFT converges faster: optimization on a smooth hypersphere manifold; targeted semantic updates
Why not minimize hyperspherical energy in finetuning (risk of destroying pretrained structure)
No inference overhead: folding R into W0 after training

outline.chapter_title: Constrained and Re-Scaled Variants: COFT and Re-Scaled OFT
outline.description: Extends OFT with explicit constraints to enhance stability (COFT) and with neuron-wise scaling to increase flexibility (re-scaled OFT), while preserving key geometric properties.
subtopics: COFT: adding a radius constraint ||R − I|| ≤ ε to bound deviation from pretrained weights
Cayley transform and Neumann series insight: moving the ε-constraint to a skew-symmetric Q and using projected gradient
Effect of ε: flexibility–stability trade-off and behavior as ε varies
Re-scaled OFT: learning a diagonal scaling D in z = (R W0 D)^T x; preserving hyperspherical energy under re-scaling
Parameter cost and practical benefits of re-scaling
Errata note regarding the placement of D in the forward pass

outline.description: Details how to implement OFT and COFT efficiently using Cayley parameterization and block-diagonal orthogonal matrices, and analyzes parameter efficiency relative to LoRA.
subtopics: Cayley parameterization: R = (I + Q)(I − Q)^{-1} with skew-symmetric Q; determinant +1 and practical impact
Block-diagonal orthogonal matrices: r blocks, optional block sharing across channels
Parameter complexity: O(d^2/r) without sharing and O(d^2/r^2) with sharing
Concrete parameter-count example (e.g., 128×128 layer) and comparison to LoRA
Computational considerations: matrix inverse cost, differentiability, and scalability
Implementation checklist: initialization (R=I via Q=0), preserving orthogonality during training

outline.chapter_title: Applying OFT Across Architectures and Pipelines
outline.description: Explains where and how to apply OFT in diffusion pipelines and across architectures, including Transformers and convolutional layers, and provides practical training guidance.
subtopics: Where to finetune: attention layers in diffusion UNet for fair comparison to LoRA
Convolutional layers: interpreting block-diagonal R as depth-wise or shared channel transforms
Integration into existing setups: DreamBooth for subject-driven, ControlNet/T2I-Adapter-style training for controllable generation
Hyperparameters: choosing r (blocks), block sharing, learning rate, optimizer, and ε for COFT
Stability tips: identity initialization, monitoring for collapse, selecting iteration counts
Compositionality potential: multiplying orthogonal matrices from different finetunings
Failure modes and troubleshooting

outline.description: Evaluates OFT and COFT on subject-driven generation using the DreamBooth framework, highlighting stability, convergence, and semantic fidelity.
subtopics: Setup: Stable Diffusion v1.5, DreamBooth loss, baselines (DreamBooth, LoRA), fair layer selection
Convergence and stability: early (≈400 iters) vs late (≈2000 iters) behavior; collapse avoidance
Quantitative metrics: DINO and CLIP-I (subject fidelity), CLIP-T (prompt fidelity), LPIPS (diversity)
Multiple-seed evaluation to reduce randomness
Key findings: superior subject preservation and prompt adherence; iteration insensitivity
Qualitative analysis: identity retention vs prompt following; representative successes and failures
Human evaluation summary and insights

outline.chapter_title: Experiments II: Controllable Generation, Metrics, and Practical Guidance
outline.description: Assesses controllable generation with new control consistency metrics, compares OFT/COFT to strong baselines, and distills practical takeaways and open problems.
subtopics: Tasks and datasets: Canny→Image (COCO), Segmentation→Image (ADE20K), Landmarks→Face (CelebA-HQ)
Control consistency metrics: edge IoU/F1, segmentation mIoU/mean/overall accuracy, landmark L2 error
Convergence comparisons: smooth, fast convergence of OFT/COFT vs sudden emergence in ControlNet
Results summary: OFT/COFT outperform ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, and LoRA; data and parameter efficiency
Qualitative outcomes: fidelity, geometry, and precise adherence to control signals
Practical guidance: picking r and ε, data requirements, iteration counts, and monitoring control metrics
Open problems: scalable orthogonalization (matrix inverse), compositionality across tasks, reducing bias from block structure
